To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combined administration of urokinase and hyaluronidases, but not the individual administration of each, reduces infarct size and the incidence of death in the isoproterenal-induced MI model in rats.

the intravenous administration (i.v.) of hyaluronase (HY) and/or urokinase alone or in combination with HY (HY+UK) reduced the infarct area and the enzyme level (increased by isoproterenole) to a varying extent.

the co-operative actions of hyaluronase and uro-kinase in the treatment of myocardial infarcted animals are due to their ability to reduce thromboxane B 2 levels and to increase the activity of plasminogen activators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the co-operative action of HY and UK on the ISP induced MI in rats.
the effect of the combined action of urokinase and hyaluronidases on the isoprotenol-induced myocardial injury in rats.
the effects of intravenous administration of HY and UK on the ISP induced MI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the co-administration of hyaluronase and urokinsin is effective in reducing the severity of experimental myocardial infarct in rats.
the co-operative action of UK and HY in the treatment of MI is due to their combined effects on the fibrinolytic activity, the TXB2 production and on the inflammatory response.
the combined administration of HY and UK is more effective than either drug given alone in reducing infarction and mortality and in normalizing the plasma TXB level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of HY and UK is more efficient than the single agents in reducing MI.
HY and UK, alone or in combination are effective in the treatment of MI in rats.
HY and UK have a complementary action in the treatment of isoproteren-induced MI in rats, and that the combination of these two agents is more effective than either one used alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combined administration of hyaluronic acid and hyaluronidases can be used to improve the efficacy of thrombolytic therapy.
hyaluronidases are a new class of therapeutic agents for the treatment of MI, which are safe, effective, and have a good potential for clinical application.
hyaluronidases and urokinases are complementary and can act synergistically in the treatment of myocardial infarctions.
